acceptance_criteria: AC-1: read the backlog note in full, OP_0B_1_COMMAND_GATE_PACKAGE.md's CP-A4 row (the model), and how CP-A4/CP-A5 are parsed and wired today; confirm the real `cphaprob tablestat` output shape from the repository's existing fixtures/docs (there is operator-supplied evidence referenced in the note) -- if no real sample exists in-repo, build the parser against the documented CCP Unique IP's Table shape and say so explicitly, fail-closed.
AC-2: add the gate row in CP-A4's exact format, marked APPROVED (Product Owner 2026-09-09).
AC-3: implement the value-free parser with the structural-skeleton diagnostic; prove by test that no IP/MAC/interface-name token from a realistic fixture survives.
AC-4: wire exactly one call per member into the existing Expert session with unchanged pacing/order; prove by test that battery order and every existing command's authority are unchanged.

AC-5: write the readiness-mapping proposal (PROPOSED, awaiting PO review) with explicit reasoning against the never-KNOWN_BAD-from-absence law, and implement it behind a named decision constant so it can be flipped without re-implementation.
AC-6: VSX/physical-VS0-only rule enforced and tested.
AC-7: update backlog note; RELAY_NOTE summarises the mapping proposal in 3-4 sentences for the Product Owner.

baseline.authority: project/backlog.json id cp_preflight_ccp_tablestat_evidence is the full specification -- its note already defines the gate row (modelled on CP-A4), the retained-field rule, the candidate readiness checks, the VSX rule and the required tests. docs/history/phase/OP_0B_1_COMMAND_GATE_PACKAGE.md is the gate-row format authority; docs/history/phase/OP_0A_HA_READINESS_ASSESSMENT.md (FROZEN) and utils/failover/assessment.py define the checks the mapping targets and the 'never KNOWN_BAD from absence' law.
baseline.sequencing: Independent of every in-flight movement. Touches checkpoint/clusterxl_preflight_provider.py, which OP.1.S1 (NXS-LOCAL-0048, running in parallel) only imports read-only -- no conflict expected, but merge origin/main before opening the PR.

context_not_loaded: Any live device contact -- the parser and wiring are proven against fixtures; the first real-battery run including tablestat is a later, Product-Owner-run real-environment step
PAN HA -- this is a Check Point ClusterXL-only evidence source
invariants: Retained fields are value-free by construction: NO IP address, NO MAC address, NO interface name survives parsing -- only bounded counts/booleans (cluster interfaces observed; interfaces where BOTH members are seen; interfaces where the peer is absent; local member seen on every required interface, cross-referenced by COUNT against CP-A4's 'Required interfaces:'). A test must prove no address/MAC token from the fixture appears anywhere in the output

Exactly one `cphaprob tablestat` call per member, in the existing per-member persistent Expert session, same INTER_COMMAND_DELAY_SECONDS pacing, NO_RETRY, CLASS_0_READ -- battery order and S4 command authority for every existing command unchanged
Physical/VS0 context only; VSX per-VS semantics are NOT established -- a VSX unit gets no per-VS tablestat call

The readiness mapping (FAIL vs INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE when the peer row is absent on a required interface) is PROPOSED with explicit reasoning against the frozen 'never KNOWN_BAD from absence' law -- the contract text must say why an absence inside the device's own positively-reported table differs from a read that produced nothing. Implement the proposed mapping behind a clearly named decision point so the Product Owner can flip it in review without a re-implementation; do not silently decide it as settled
Structural-skeleton diagnostic on unrecognised shape; parser fails closed, never guesses
report.merge_gate: Standing relay#13: green tests -> self-merge, report via RELAY_NOTE. Because the readiness mapping is a Product Owner review item, the RELAY_NOTE must state the proposed mapping and its reasoning in three or four sentences so it can be accepted or flipped on read.

Deliver (1) the new command-gate row, (2) a value-free parser retaining counts/booleans only, (3) a PROPOSED readiness-contract mapping written for Product Owner review, and (4) the wiring, exactly per the backlog note's five 'WHAT IMPLEMENTATION NEEDS' points.

Parser in checkpoint/clusterxl_preflight_provider.py (or its parsing sibling, following where CP-A4/CP-A5 parsers live) emitting only the bounded counts/booleans above, with the structural-skeleton diagnostic
